releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.1
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.1 makes `pnpm install` work in StackBlitz WebContainers, repairs lockfiles whose patch hashes disagree with `patchedDependencies`, and fixes many bugs in Windows command shims, injected workspace dependencies, and `pnpm deploy`.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

* `pnpm install` now works in StackBlitz WebContainers. On projects without a lockfile, it used to fail with `ENOENT ... pnpm-lock.yaml`, because pnpm did not recognize the errors that WebContainers return from asynchronous file system calls. It also failed with "this.db.exec is not a function", because `node:sqlite` there lacks `DatabaseSync.exec`. When `node:sqlite` cannot prepare statements either, pnpm stores the index in `index.fallback` [#15649](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/15649).

* `pnpm install` now completes after downloading a Node.js runtime specified by `devEngines.runtime` when pnpm runs on Node.js 24.4.x [#14667](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14667).

* `pnpm install` no longer fails when a package from the registry declares a `file:` dependency on a directory inside itself, such as `"@types/css-tree": "file:./typings/css-tree"`. pnpm links that dependency to the directory inside the package, as npm and Yarn do. The lockfile records it as `link:<root>/typings/css-tree` [#9141](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9141).

* Installing a git-hosted dependency that has to be built no longer fails when that dependency's own dependencies have build scripts nobody approved. pnpm skips those builds while preparing the dependency, as it does without `strictDepBuilds` [#9764](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9764).

* pnpm now uses pnpm to prepare a git-hosted dependency that is a pnpm workspace without a committed lockfile. It used npm before, which could skip the dependency's build [#14011](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14011).

* When installing a git dependency over SSH fails with `Permission denied (publickey)`, pnpm suggests checking the loaded keys with `ssh-add -l`. Resolving an SSH URL that refuses the key also shows a local HTTPS rewrite that leaves the recorded URL alone [#13743](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13743).

* `pnpm install --dev` and `pnpm fetch --dev` now install the optional dependencies of devDependencies, such as the platform binaries of Biome and oxlint. The project's own `optionalDependencies` are still skipped [#9678](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9678).

* `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now works on a detached HEAD when `gitBranchLockfile` is enabled. The install now reads the lockfiles of the local and remote-tracking branches that contain the checked-out commit. It still writes the shared `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#7672](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7672).

* `pnpm install` on CI now fails on an outdated lockfile when `preferFrozenLockfile` is explicitly set to `true`. Setting it to `true` used to let CI update the lockfile [#9072](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9072).

* `pnpm install` now

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.8
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.8.0 warns when `pnpm pack` or `pnpm publish` would ship a `.env` file that `files` does not list, installs `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` workspaces concurrently, applies every setting passed as `--config.<name>=<value>`, and no longer leaves the Windows terminal stuck after Ctrl+C in a script.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now warn when the tarball includes a `.env` or `.env.*` file that the `files` field of `package.json` does not list. Templates such as `.env.example` are not reported. List the file in `files` to publish it on purpose, or exclude it in `.npmignore` or `.gitignore` [#7826](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7826).

- `pnpm pack` now honors `--silent`, `--reporter=silent`, and `--loglevel=silent` to hide the tarball contents and summary. With `--json`, lifecycle script output and the final JSON output remain visible [#10297](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10297).

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

- Installing through a `pnpr` server now records the pnpmfile checksum in the lockfile, so a later `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts that lockfile [#14460](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14460). A frozen install through the pnpr server now fails if the pnpmfile changed. If the pnpmfile defines a `readPackage`, `afterAllResolved` or `preResolution` hook or custom resolvers, pnpm resolves dependencies locally and prints a warning that the pnpr server was not used.

  Installing through a `pnpr` server also links a workspace project at the directory its `publishConfig.directory` names. A server that does not forward the setting makes the install fail with `ERR_PNPM_PNPR_PUBLISH_DIRECTORY_MISMATCH`, so pnpm never writes a lockfile that points at the wrong directory. The server rejects a `publishConfig.directory` that points outside its project.

- Installing a git-hosted dependency that has to be built no longer fails when that dependency's own dependencies have build scripts nobody approved. pnpm skips those builds while preparing the dependency, as it does without `strictDepBuilds` [#9764](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9764).

- A git-hosted dependency that is a pnpm workspace with no committed lockfile is now detected as a pnpm project [#14011](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14011).

- `pnpm install --dev` and `pnpm fetch --dev` now install the optional dependencies of devDependencies, such as the platform binaries of Biome and oxlint. The project's own `optionalDependencies` are still skipped [#9678](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9678).

- `pnpm install --offline` and `pnpm add --offline` now resolve a version range to the newest matching version whose tarball is already in the store. They used to pick the newest version in the cached metadata and fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL` when its tarball was missing [#10715](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10715).

- If an offline install fails because the registry metadata cache uses the layout from befo

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.8.1
releasesInRange.body: pnpm 12.8.1 fixes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting lockfiles with injected workspace packages that have peers, restores the executable bit on files of local directory dependencies, makes `pnpm dedupe` converge, and uses less CPU on many-core machines. ### Patch Changes - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer rejects a freshly generated lockfile when an injected workspace package has peer dependencies [#16332](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16332). - Executable files in a `file:` directory dependency or an injected workspace package keep their executable bit again. Since 12.8.0, pnpm installed these files without the permissions they have in their project. - `pnpm dedupe` now reaches a stable lockfile when a package's peer suffix is long enough to be hashed. Before, each run could switch that package's key between the hashed and the spelled-out suffix, so `pnpm dedupe --check` always failed [#16331](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16331). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, the default in CI, now uses less CPU on machines with more than 8 cores. Warm installs on many-core Windows machines got up to 10% faster. Frozen installs now link with at most 16 worker threads. - `verifyDepsBeforeRun` no longer reports dependencies as outdated after a filtered install just because `pnpm-lock.yaml` has a newer modification time. It checks the lockfile against the packages that install put in place. Before, `pnpm run` reinstalled the whole workspace with lifecycle scripts on, for example after a Docker `COPY` brought in a lockfile with a newer mtime [#16322](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16322). After a filtered install, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now also checks that the install put the selected projects' dependencies in place. A `node_modules` directory alone no longer counts as proof. - `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer install a project that has never been installed and has nothing to install. Such a project declares no dependencies, no peer dependencies that `autoInstallPeers` would fetch, and no install lifecycle scripts. The command now runs without writing `node_modules` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#16313](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16313). - `pnpm update -g --latest` now upgrades globally installed packages beyond their saved version ranges [#16320](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16320). ## Platinum Sponsors

Before, `pnpm run` reinstalled the whole workspace with lifecycle scripts on, for example after a Docker `COPY` brought in a lockfile with a newer mtime [#16322](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16322). After a filtered install, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now also checks that the install put the selected projects' dependencies in place. A `node_modules` directory alone no longer counts as proof. * `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer install a project that has never been installed and has nothing to install. Such a project declares no dependencies, no peer dependencies that `autoInstallPeers` would fetch, and no install lifecycle scripts. The command now runs without writing `node_modules` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#16313](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16313). ## Platinum Sponsors

releasesInRange.body:
### Patch Changes * e7888e5: `pnpm self-update` now resolves and verifies pnpm through registry, authentication, proxy, and TLS settings from trusted non-project configuration. Project configuration and the default project pnpmfile can no longer redirect the pnpm download or disable engine identity verification. * 46bc7c9: pnpm no longer tells you to update itself with Corepack or with `pnpm add -g`: * The update notification now suggests `pnpm self-update`, or the [standalone install script](https://pnpm.io/installation) when pnpm is running under Corepack. prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
`create_dir_all_inheriting_mode` and `inherited_dir_bits` are documented on every platform, but their doc comments linked to `grant_inherited_dir_mode`, which is `#[cfg(unix)]`. rustdoc resolves intra-doc links only in the code compiled for the target, so on Windows the links are broken and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --document-private-items` fails. That breaks the pre-push hook (`pnpm/scripts/pre-push-rust.sh`) for anyone pushing from Windows.

CI didn't catch it because the `Rust CI / Doc` job ran on Ubuntu only, where the function exists.

Writing the name unlinked doesn't work: on Linux, dylint's `bare_identifier_reference` requires an in-scope name to be an intra-doc link, and that same link fails rustdoc on Windows. Doc comments only; no behavior change.
- The doc job gets the same Ubuntu + Windows matrix as Clippy, so a link like this fails in CI. The required `Rust CI / Success` gate depends on the job id `doc`, so renaming the check to `Rust CI / Doc / <os>` doesn't affect branch protection.

prs.title: fix(deps-restorer): keep the modes of local-directory dependency files
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm 12.8.0 installs a file of a `file:` directory dependency, or of an injected workspace package, without its executable bit. pnpm/pnpm#15646 made the importer materialize every file at the mode a fresh store write under the current umask would produce, and it takes executability from the CAS `-exec` suffix. A local-directory dependency is imported from its project's own files, which never carry that suffix, so a `0755` script lands as `0644`. A hardlink falls back to that copy too, because the project file's mode never matches the store-entry mode it is compared against.

This surfaced in pnpm/pnpm#15869, where bumping the repo's `packageManager` to 12.8.0 makes two `pnpm/npm/pnpm/test/install.test.mjs` cases fail with `EACCES`: the fixture's native binary is a `file:` optional dependency.

The fix ports pnpm 11's `isCafsFile` check. Only a source with the CAFS layout `files/<2 hex>/<digest>[-exec]` gets the store-entry mode. Any other source keeps its own mode and can be hardlinked whatever that mode is. pnpm 11 already behaves this way, so it needs no change.

Reproduction on Linux, umask `022`: a `file:../dep` dependency whose `run` is `0755` installs as `-rwxr-xr-x` with 12.7.0 and as `-rw-r--r--` with 12.8.0. With this branch it is `-rwxr-xr-x` again.

prs.author: neonsid
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` spawn an install when no workspace state file exists. For a project that has nothing to install, that install only writes `node_modules` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`. After pnpm/pnpm#15125, this became visible in directories that the workspace `packages` patterns leave out (pnpm/pnpm#16313). The same was already true for any standalone scripts-only project.

The verify-deps gate now reports "up to date" when no state file exists and no project the install would cover has install work. Install work means any of these:

- a required peer, when `autoInstallPeers` is on;
- an install lifecycle script (`preinstall` through `postprepare`, or the implicit `node-gyp rebuild` for a `binding.gyp`), unless `ignoreScripts` is set. `pnpm:devPreinstall` counts only in the workspace root. prs.title: fix(deps-resolver): pin the same peers for hashed and explicit suffixes
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16331.

`pnpm dedupe` alternated between two lockfiles when a package's peer suffix was long enough to be hashed. The locked peer pins read from the wanted lockfile differed depending on whether a key was spelled out or hashed. An explicit suffix pins every segment, including peers a descendant resolved, and recurses into each provider's own suffix. A hashed suffix recovered only the package's declared peers.

In the reported workspace, two importers produce equally sized variants of `@react-native-firebase/app`, and `dedupe_peer_dependents` breaks the tie by dep path, sometimes toward the hashed spelling. From the hashed spelling, the next run lost the transitive `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` pin for one importer. That shrank its variant, flipped the collapse winner and the key spelling, and the cycle repeated.

A hashed suffix now recovers the same pins: the peers listed in the snapshot's `transitivePeerDependencies`, read from the descendants that declare them, plus each peer provider's own peers. A visited set bounds both walks.

pnpm v11 is not affected. It never resolves `@react-native-firebase/app` in this workspace under `autoInstallPeers: false`, and a fresh pnpm v12 resolve doesn't either. The variants only exist because v12 keeps peers the existing lockfile pinned.

Not addressed here: after `dedupe_peer_dependents` rewrites a surviving variant's edges, its hashed key can still encode the peer it had before the rewrite. Th

prs.title: fix: recursive install skipping every project when the repository root is the filesystem root
prs.author: cnZary
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16328.

For a workspace with a shared lockfile, the recursive installer (`pnpm install`/`add`/`remove`/`update`/`import`) filters the selected importers with `is-subdir` against the calculated repository root. `is-subdir@2.0.0` appends a path separator to the resolved parent directory, so when that root is the filesystem root the parent becomes `//` on POSIX or `C:\\` on Windows, and no real project path starts with it. Every importer is filtered out, and the command reports success (`Scope: all N workspace projects` / `Done`) without installing anything.

The fix ships in `is-subdir@2.0.1`, which no longer appends a second separator when the parent already ends with one, and this PR takes the bump (with a changeset). Cross-volume exclusion on Windows and path resolution semantics are unchanged.

Only the TypeScript pnpm v11 CLI is affected; the reporter's matrix and my own check on Windows show pnpm 12 (pacquet) handles both layouts correctly, so per the repo's version policy only v11 is fixed.

In addition to the reporter's POSIX case, this reproduces on Windows when the projects' common ancestor is a drive root (e.g. an app at `C:\app` with workspace members at `C:\external\projects/*`), which the issue's reproduction script explicitly excludes. Verified before/after on this layout.

prs.title: fix: accept a touched lockfile in verifyDepsBeforeRun after a filtered install
prs.author: neonsid
prs.body:
## Summary

Close pnpm/pnpm#16322

After a filtered install, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` treated the dependencies as outdated as soon as `pnpm-lock.yaml` got a newer mtime than `lastValidatedTimestamp`, even with byte-identical contents. With the default `install` action, `pnpm run` then reinstalled the whole workspace with scripts on. The issue hits this in Docker multi-stage builds, where the root `prepare` fails for lack of git.

**Root cause.** When the wanted lockfile is newer than the last validation, both stacks assert that it equals the current lockfile in `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml`. A filtered install only materializes the projects it selected, so its current lockfile never has the packages of the other projects. That makes the equality impossible, and the gate fails with "the installed dependencies are not up to date with the lockfile". The mtime check is fine. The comparison that runs after it is wrong for filtered installs.

**Fix.** When the workspace state records `filteredInstall`, the gate compares the current lockfile against what that install actually put in place:

- pnpm v12 builds the materialization closure of the wanted lockfile rooted at the importers the current lockfile lists (`materialization_closure`, the same function the install uses), then compares.
- pnpm v11's current lockfile keeps every importer and drops only packages. So `assertLockfilesEqual` accepts it when everything except `packages` is equal and every package it records equals the wante
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(deps-resolver): dedupe injected workspace deps after peer variants merge
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a fresh `pnpm install` recorded some workspace dependencies in `importers` as peer-suffixed `file:` copies where pnpm 11 records `link:`.

The injected copy resolves an optional peer (`supports-color` for `debug` in both fixtures) from its consumer, while the target project's own dependencies were walked without it. pnpm 12 ran the injected-deps dedupe *before* peer-dependent dedupe, so it compared the injected children with the project's peer-free variants, found no match, and kept the `file:` copy. Peer-dependent dedupe later merged those variants anyway, which is why `pnpm dedupe` on an existing lockfile removed the copies.

This PR runs peer-dependent dedupe first. The injected copy's children then equal the project's direct deps and the edge becomes `link:`.

This differs from pnpm/pnpm#16299, which made the child check accept an injected child that carries *more* peers than the project. That would link an injected copy whose peer context is genuinely richer than the project's. Reordering only links edges whose variants peer-dependent dedupe already treats as interchangeable.

pnpm 11 does not have the bug (its peer cache hands the project the same variants), so this is a v12-only fix.

Verified against both fixtures from the issue with `install --lockfile-only`:
- `omril1/pnpm-dedupe-link-injection-repro` (`spurious-suffix/`): lockfile is byte-identical to pnpm 11.28.2.

prs.author: arturict
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16355

With `cargo.enabled: true`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeded even when `Cargo.lock` no longer satisfied a dependency requirement in `Cargo.toml`. `cargo --locked` rejected the same pair right afterwards with exit code 101.

**Root cause.** `read_or_resolve_lockfile` returns an existing `Cargo.lock` as it is. Nothing compared it with the workspace manifests, so `--frozen-lockfile` only checked that the file exists.

Error:   × Cargo.lock is out of date, but --frozen-lockfile forbids updating it
  ╰─▶ app depends on demo =1.0.1, but Cargo.lock locks demo 1.0.0

On a Linux system with no CA certificates, such as `node:24-slim`, setting `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` made registry requests fail with `UnknownIssuer`. `rustls-platform-verifier` only rejects an empty system store when it gets no extra roots. ```text
rustls-platform-verifier only fails on an empty system trust store when
it gets no extra roots. With NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS set, the extra CA kept
the platform client buildable on a system without CA certificates, so
the bundled-roots fallback never ran and the client trusted only that
CA. Registry requests then failed with UnknownIssuer.

Build the platform client without the extra roots first, and fall back

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Git-hosted dependencies now respect `pmOnFail`. Closes pnpm/pnpm#16376.

When a git-hosted dependency pins a pnpm version (`packageManager: pnpm@x`), pnpm prepares it by running `pnpm dlx --package pnpm@x pnpm install`. It did this even when the install ran with `--pm-on-fail=ignore`. On NixOS the downloaded generic binary cannot start, and `pmOnFail=ignore` is how users keep the nixpkgs build. As a result, such dependencies could not be installed at all.

With this PR, the install's `pmOnFail` reaches the git fetcher:

- If it is set to anything other than `download`, a dependency that wants pnpm gets a `pnpm` shim that runs the running pnpm directly. Nothing is downloaded.

With `error` or `warn`, the nested install applies that policy to the dependency's pin. It fails or warns instead of downloading the pinned pnpm. Pins for other package managers (npm, Yarn, Bun) are unaffected.

pnpm v11 does not provision package managers for git-hosted dependencies, so the fix is v12-only.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, `pnpm deploy` fails with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` when a workspace package lists its peer as a dev dependency too and the deployed graph holds a second version of that peer.

The cause is not the hard-coded `injectWorkspacePackages: false` in the deploy manifest the issue points at, which is intended: the injected snapshots are copied into the deploy lockfile. The actual chain:

1. `dedupeInjectedDeps` turns an injected workspace dependency into `link:` when the injected children are a subset of the target project's importer, **dev dependencies included**. So a package whose peer is also its dev dependency is linked, not injected.
2. Deploy synthesizes the snapshot of a linked workspace package from its importer's prod/optional dependencies only, so that peer binding is lost.
3. `bindSingletonPeers` then sees every version of the peer in the deployed graph and throws.

In an injected workspace, deploy now binds such a peer to the package's own dev-dependency resolution, but only when the deployed graph contains it. Dedupe guarantees this is the resolution the injected snapshot would have carried. Non-injected workspaces keep the existing behavior (bind what injection would choose, refuse when ambiguous). An existing v12 test depends on that: `lib`'s dev dependency is a different version there.

## Summary

On macOS and Linux, lifecycle scripts and `pnpm run` now always get `PATH` from the `PATH` variable. Before, a `Path` variable could supply it.

prs.title: fix(resolver): let a too-new latest fall back to a prerelease of its major
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

When `minimumReleaseAge` hides the version a stable dist-tag points to, the tag was only allowed to move to other stable versions. For a package that shipped `1.0.0` after months of `1.0.0-beta.x` releases tagged `latest`, `latest` fell back to `0.0.1` during the release-age window (see cloudflare/vinext#3567, where `pnpm create vinext-app@latest` failed with `ERR_PNPM_DLX_NO_BIN`).

Candidates for a dropped tag are now ranked in tiers, compared before the version:

1. same prerelease-ness as the target, on its major (unchanged)
2. a prerelease of the stable target's major, below the target (new)
3. same prerelease-ness on a lower major, `latest` only (unchanged)

Non-deprecated versions still win over deprecated ones. Without a tier-2 candidate the tiers follow version order, so nothing else changes. A stable version of the same major still beats a prerelease (`1.5.0` too new → `1.4.0`, not `1.5.0-rc.1`).

The bug is in both stacks: fixed in the Rust resolver (`best_tag_candidate`) and in v11's `filterPkgMetadataVersions`.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16388

1.0.0 fell back to an ancient 0.0.1 even though 1.0.0-beta.4 had been

## Summary

On Unix, pnpm v12 keeps its per-user lock files in `/tmp`. Those are the store operation locks, the directory-lock held files, and the verify-deps install locks. A sandbox that only allows writes to a per-session directory, such as the macOS Seatbelt profiles coding agents use, therefore can't run any command that touches the store (`ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_OPEN_OPERATION_LOCK`).

This PR puts that lock root in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when the variable holds an absolute path to a directory the current effective user owns, which is the issue's main proposal. The ownership check covers `su` and `sudo --preserve-env`, which pass on the caller's `/run/user/<uid>`. A directory that the owner cannot write to, or that other users can write to, is also rejected. In the second case another user could rename a held lock directory or pre-create one. Without the variable it stays in `/tmp` (on Android, `HOME/.cache`). `TMPDIR` is still ignored on purpose, because it varies per process. Windows is unchanged and keeps using `LocalAppData`.

The trade-off: two processes coordinate only if they resolve the same directory. So a process with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (a login shell) and one without it (a cron job running `pnpm store prune`) no longer wait for each other. On Linux, login sessions all get the same `/run/user/<uid>`, so this only affects processes that run outside a session. The storeDir docs now say this.

This is v12 only. pnpm v11 has no store operation locks.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#1639
